status: provisional — pending owner/TLF decisions D3 (transport), D4 (receipt), D5 (scopes), D8 (human approval); not an adopted profile

transport.binding: RFC 9421 HTTP Message Signatures, one signature labelled 'aria'
transport.label: aria
transport.nonce: a single-use receiver challenge, fresh for every request, lookups included

headers.aria-credential: sf-string: the exact credential document URL, with parameter digest=:<sha-256 of its canonical JSON>:
headers.aria-audience: sf-string: the receiver DID the request is for
headers.aria-operation: sf-string: the logical operation id (UUID), the same on every retry

identity.response: the receiver's credential document and a statement: type, subject, credential, origin, audience, nonce, challenge, created, proof { alg, keyid, value }; exactly these members
identity.signed: the ARIA canonical JSON of the statement with proof.value removed (proof.alg and proof.keyid are signed); strict Ed25519 by the named credential's holder key
order: malformed: the members above and no others; type; strings; nonce and challenge syntax; origin canonical (https://host[:port], or http:// on a loopback host; it serializes as a URL to itself, valid IDNA included); created RFC 3339 UTC to the second, a date that exists
credential: the presented document verifies now under the client's trusted issuers, and is the credential the statement names, of the statement's subject
unexpected_receiver: the subject is the pinned DID
origin: the origin is the pinned origin; a pin outside the origin rule matches no statement
stale: created <= now + skew and now - created <= 60 s
signature: proof.alg ed25519, proof.keyid the credential's holderKey.id, a canonical 64-byte value, strict Ed25519
status: the credential's status establishes it stands now
stale: judged again once status is established
identity.use: a verified receiver keeps its credential, status evidence and statement deadline; signing a request for it judges, at entry and again after the signer returns, the statement deadline and the credential's standing, and refuses a request whose own signature window ended while it was signed. A recorded receipt is not reinterpreted when its receiver later lapses.

retrieval.refusals: problem documents, unsigned: a retrieval produces no receipt

semanticHeaders: every semantic header the descriptor declares and the request carries is covered after the class components, and enters the fingerprint
authenticationOrder: 400 aria.request_invalid: a supported method and exactly one described operation (method and exact path); the target is taken as sent: appended to the configured origin it must serialize as a URL to the same text, so dot segments and other spellings a parser would normalise are refused
400: body rules of the class; for unsafe-body, the descriptor's one media type after normalisation
400: only declared query parameters, each at most once; retrieval names one operation UUID
400: ARIA-Operation exactly once as a UUID sf-string on receiptable classes, absent on retrieval
401 signature: exactly one signature, labelled aria
401 unsigned_operation | digest | signature: covered components are exactly the required ones, without parameters or repeats
401 signature | window: parameters exactly created, expires, nonce, keyid, alg, tag; window at most 60 s and current within the skew (created <= now + skew and expires >= now - skew)
401 digest: Content-Digest sha-256 of the exact content, its bytes spelled canonically
401 challenge: the nonce is a challenge this receiver issued, unconsumed and live strictly before its expiry (refused at the expiry instant)

401 credential: the exact credential named, verifying now (an expired or not yet valid credential is refused here), its digest spelled canonically and equal, keyid equal to its holderKey.id, the key acceptable

401 signature: every covered field present exactly once (a repeated field is refused, never combined), the signature bytes spelled canonically, strict Ed25519 over the base rebuilt from the receiver's configured origin
401 window: the window judged again after the credential is resolved and the signature verified
the challenge is consumed atomically; 401 window: judged again after consumption (the challenge stays consumed); the request is authenticated
403 aria.audience_mismatch: the first admission check (signed rejected/attempt, or a problem document for retrieval)
encodings: every byte sequence (signature, Content-Digest, the aria-credential digest, a proof value) is accepted only in its canonical spelling: sf-binary is padded base64 with zero trailing bits, a proof value is unpadded base64url with zero trailing bits; another spelling of the same bytes is refused by the check that reads it
ed25519: holder key canonical, not small order, torsion free; R canonical, not small order, torsion free; S < L; then RFC 8032 verification (both equations then agree)

fingerprint.algorithm: sha-256 over the ARIA canonical JSON of the object below, written sha-256=:<base64>:

object.path: the exact path, without the query
object.query: object of the descriptor's query parameters present, name to value
object.mediaType: the descriptor's one media type, lowercase, parameters sorted (unsafe-body only)
object.semanticHeaders: object of the descriptor's semantic headers present, lowercase name to value
object.contentDigest: RFC 9530 sha-256 of the body; of empty content for unsafe-empty; absent for safe classes

receipt.signed: the ARIA canonical JSON of the receipt with proof.value removed (proof.alg and proof.keyid are signed)
receipt.dataModel: objects, strings and integers only; no duplicate keys; no unknown members

aria.authentication_failed.note: challenge covers replay: a consumed challenge is refused; credential covers a credential already expired or not yet valid when presented

aria.credential_expired.note: the credential authenticated, then its validity ended before admission or before the admission was used

aria.operation_unknown.note: retrieval of an operation with no record; the client keeps it unknown

receiverReasons: namespaced <ns>.<name>: resource authorization in admission (403, attempt), business rules after the claim (422, operation)

atpMapping.ATP-200: admission allow (flagged in monitor/warn); never a receipt state
atpMapping.ATP-401/EXPIRED: expired when presented: aria.authentication_failed (credential), 401 unsigned; validity ended between authentication and admission: aria.credential_expired, 403 signed rejected/attempt

scopes: D5 provisional: new grants are namespace:resource:action, three lowercase segments, no @version; 1.0 documents are read under their own pattern (two or more segments); credential scopes compare exactly, never as patterns; receiver policy patterns may end in :* and a matching deny wins
approval: D8 provisional: refuse — a missing approval rejects the attempt and claims nothing; holding for approval is deferred
reconciliation: an uncertain failure marks the claim, by compare-and-set, and keeps it locked; a release names the exact claim observed and an assurance that the old work cannot apply its effect later (transactional: the effect commits only with its recorded outcome; fenced: an external adapter guarantees final absence and that the old work cannot commit); an unmarked claim, a missing assurance or an observation of an earlier claim releases nothing; effects are counted when they land, apart from the record
admissionLifetime: an admission is judged when made and again when used: after the resource authorizer, before a claim is granted or a stored result is read, and after every storage wait, on every path that returns a result (a new claim, an existing record, a lost create race, a resumed operation); it keeps its status evidence and approval and expires with its request (signature expires plus skew); a lookup is judged again before and after its read. A lapsed admission is refused or expires without changing the recorded outcome or its receipts
revocationLookup: D4 provisional: a revoked credential authorizes no lookup; a currently valid credential of the same DID may retrieve the original receipt; revocation never deletes or reclassifies the operation

historicalReceipts.evidence: the receipt, the client's kept attempts, the retained document of the exact receiver credential the receipt names, and optionally a retained status list
historicalReceipts.authenticity: the document verifies under a trusted issuer as at verification (schema, issuer, proof, both signatures, holder key, rules, level, trusted list), except against the current time; a list verifies as when fetched (issuer, the exact list the credential names, both signatures, supported subject, at most 24 h), its times reported, not judged
order: evidence_missing: no authentic document of the credential the receipt names
historicalReceipts.findings: issuedAtWithinValidity (validFrom inclusive, validUntil exclusive); retainedStatus active | revoked | not_retained, with the list's period; signingTime receiver_claim. Reported, never folded into validity
historicalReceipts.authorization: none: historical authenticity is never current standing; nothing that admits, signs or tracks accepts it
